correctness.rationale: The exact determinant and trace are verified symbolically. The invertible translation/time rescaling gives a polynomial harmonic oscillator; second-order solutions and third-order cos/sin resonances have exact computed coefficients. They uniquely imply \(m=1/(4s^2)\) and \(\omega_2=-(9s^4-5s^2+1)/(24s^4)\). A separate full cubic near-identity complex normal-form calculation gives \(c_{21}=-1/(8s^3)+i(9s^4-5s^2+1)/(24s^4)\), proving nondegenerate supercritical Hopf. With parameter transversality this supports a genuine unique small stable orbit and the O_s(mu^2) period remainder, rather than mere formal numerics. Exact checker verifies all equations and the sharp identity \(C(s)=(1+(3s-s^{-1})^2)/6\) >=1/6. Domain \(0<s<1\), positive a,b, and local quantifiers are explicit; the computation does not assert any global cycle monotonicity.

originality.rationale: Closest directly matching full text, Liu–Shi–Wang–Feng (2013), Section 2, obtains the same kinetic Hopf surface and stable-cycle direction (Theorem 2.2), but states only the leading period \(2\pi/s+o(1)\) and the real Lyapunov coefficient, not the derivative of physical period along the fixed-determinant trace path or its unique sharp minimum. Exact novelty is the nontrivial parameter-wide period coefficient and optimal lower bound, rather than the Hopf theorem, Fourier method, or cubic-normal-form machinery. Schnakenberg (1979) and Kusbeyzi Aybar et al. (2021) are potentially relevant; their accessible abstracts and previews do not imply the claim, but full-text gaps leave priority uncertainty. Al Noufaey (2021) calculates Lindstedt–Poincaré frequency shifts in diffusion-dependent Galerkin approximations with conversion-rate variation, not the exact homogeneous constant-determinant feed path.
residual_risks: The complete 1979 founding paper and especially the same-model 2021 limit-cycle chapter were not accessible in full; an unrecognized earlier near-Hopf period calculation remains possible.

value.rationale: The least period is a physically meaningful dynamical invariant on an entire natural family of three-reaction kinetic Hopf points. Varying b-a at fixed a+b holds the equilibrium determinant (linear frequency scale) fixed and isolates the nonlinear phase response. The exact sign and sharp globally optimized normalized slope \(C(s)\ge1/6\) at \(s=1/\sqrt3\) distinguish a feasible feed balance for near-onset period sensitivity. Neither the mere supercriticality sign nor trace/determinant gives this invariant; the nonzero minimum and unique optimizer provide a substantive boundary for local frequency control. The claim is a genuine parameter-wide calculation, not a finite table, an arbitrary slice, or a renaming. The only asserted implication is local, with historical-risk qualification.
